action_items: OPTIONAL: Update /app/backend/tests/test_iteration2.py::TestUpload::test_upload_rejects_non_image — it asserts that a .txt upload returns 400, but iter4 intentionally added 'txt' (and pdf/doc/docx/xls/xlsx/dwg) to MIME_BY_EXT, so this test now fails. Replace the rejected extension with something truly unsupported (e.g. '.exe' or '.zip') so the regression suite is green.

OPTIONAL: 'Test Doc' (1 KB) was present in client_documents at the start of this iteration — likely orphaned from a previous manual or automated test that didn't clean up. I removed it during cleanup. Consider adding a teardown fixture in the main agent's manual test scripts, or seed only when count==0 already handles future seeds correctly.
critical_code_review_comments: server.py list_documents: when a client passes cp_id that IS in their allowed list, the function builds query['cp_id'] = {'$in': allowed} if not cp_id else cp_id — works, but the conditional is a bit obscure. A cleaner refactor: after the 403 check, simply set query['cp_id'] = cp_id when provided, else query['cp_id'] = {'$in': allowed}.

server.py upload_file MIME table: 'dwg' is mapped to 'application/acad' which is non-standard. The IANA registration is 'image/vnd.dwg'. Low impact since only file_type metadata is affected, not actual rendering.

server.py create_document does not validate that file_url is reachable or that file_type matches an allowed MIME. Admin-only endpoint so risk is low, but consider Pydantic url validation (HttpUrl) for file_url to catch typos at the API boundary.

server.py delete_document does NOT physically delete the underlying object-storage blob — only the metadata row in client_documents. If admin uploaded a 5MB DWG via /api/upload then attached via /api/client/documents, deleting the document row leaves the blob orphaned. Consider linking client_documents to files.file_id and soft-deleting both.

server.py on_startup: db.login_attempts.delete_many({'failed_at': {'$type': 'string'}}) runs every startup — fine for migration but could be moved behind a one-time guard once production data is migrated.

ProjectDetail.jsx (verified via UI): related-projects filter appears to be by category — confirm it excludes the current project itself (the screenshot showed only 1 related residential project beside Maple Ridge — looks correct, but with only 2 residential seeds total this is an edge case).

Dashboard.jsx (DocumentRow): client view hides trash icon correctly; admin view shows both download and trash. Good. Consider also showing the uploader/admin name + uploaded_at relative-time ('2 days ago') for clarity.
